instruments.evidence: Ran the public thumbnail gate against a real migrated Postgres for the first time, through every state it exists to refuse. It holds: an unpublished thumbnail is refused, a published one is readable signed-in and anonymous, a banned author's is refused, a blocked viewer's is refused, and it agrees with the asset path it shares a gate with. Also queried the live gallery for likeness candidates carrying a thumbnail: none exist, so grid-R1 orphaned nothing in practice.
Nothing model-facing changed this pass. The thumbnails produced by the unchanged pipeline were run for real and looked at during the previous ledger, including one fetched back out of R2.
The new test reads OmniChatThumbnailSuffix rather than spelling '-thumb', so an assertion about what was NOT uploaded cannot drift away from what is uploaded.

instruments.why: No shape crossing to a client changed.

instruments.evidence: Two readers of one rule: commitFor decides where a render is stored and MakesAGalleryAsset decides whether it gets a tile image. A test now requires them to agree for all five modes rather than trusting two switches to stay in step.

instruments.why: No provider or worker contract in scope.
No field added to a struct that crosses a boundary.
No untyped or reflective accessor in scope.

instruments.evidence: Found a stale fixture: the deletion test still spelled out '<job id>-thumb.jpg' two commits after the writer moved to naming the whole asset file, so it passed while describing a key that no longer existed. Corrected to build the key with the function that writes it. Not recorded as a finding, because reverting the correction produces no failure -- the old literal is a valid key too -- and by this review's own rule a control that passes means the finding is about the test, not the product.
MakesAGalleryAsset accepts the three modes that really write an asset, asserted against commitFor's own routing rather than against a list written twice.
The two modes that must be refused a thumbnail are driven through a whole job, and every uploaded key is checked for the suffix.
An unrecognised mode falls to the same default in both readers, so the two cannot disagree about one.
Compared the thumbnail against the asset it stands beside: the asset is a media_files row that the outbox trigger sees, and the thumbnail is not. That asymmetry is grid-R1.
The image branch of storeThumbnail is still reached by ordinary stills; the early return is reached by the two likeness modes; both exercised.
The new early return logs nothing, deliberately: it is the normal path for two modes, and a warning on every likeness render is a warning nobody reads.
The thumbnail is now gated on the mode, and the gate is the same one the storage destination uses.
The gallery-asset rule was implicit in commitFor's switch and its comment. It is a named method now, read by both.

The shape is 'a derived object stored beside a media_files row, which the row's deletion trigger cannot see'. Looked for others: the playback rendition replaces the asset in place rather than adding an object; the HLS transcode writes a directory of them and would have the same problem, but nothing enqueues it, so it is not live; ordinary upload thumbnails are outside the omnichat retention path entirely. No second live instance.
The mode check happens before any upload, so a refused thumbnail leaves no partial state.

This is what found grid-R1. Asking what is left behind when a likeness pick discards three of four candidates: the discard is a DELETE on media_files, the outbox trigger hands over that row's storage_path, and a thumbnail is not a media_files row.

One control built and replayed by hand; it produces a named assertion failure on both likeness modes. A second control was built for the stale fixture and PASSED, which is why that was withdrawn as a finding rather than written up.
MakesAGalleryAsset is invoked by the thumbnail path and asserted against commitFor, so it cannot become a rule nobody reads.
